security_audit.summary: The 400 static matches are predominantly scanner false positives: lockfile integrity hashes, ordinary key identifiers, documentation, and bounded workflow tooling. No hidden payload, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or command injection was found in the reviewed context. The optional installer persistently modifies user-level Claude Code hook configuration and should require explicit informed consent. Static review was capped at 400/1755 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1355 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The optional installer changes user-level Claude Code settings.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact settings change, create a backup, and require a clear confirmation before writing the hook configuration.

remediation.issue: The upgrade command downloads and replaces template files from an upstream reference.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict upgrades to immutable commit hashes or signed releases, display the target revision, and retain the existing confirmation gate.

remediation.issue: The workflow runner launches local processes and can use environment-held provider credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the allow-listed child environment and document every forwarded credential and external provider destination.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent global hook installation
semantic_findings.description: The optional installer writes PreToolUse hooks into the user-level Claude Code settings file. This creates persistent command interception outside an individual workflow project and warrants explicit informed consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly instructs users to run the installer, and the installer writes hook entries to ~/.claude/settings.json. The behavior is transparent and opt-in, but it is persistent global configuration.

content.value_statement: Reusable GTM work needs consistent setup, testing, approvals, and run tracking. This skill creates and maintains workflow projects with cost-aware checks and deployment steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates a workflow project from the included template when one is absent.
Drafts workflow code, result tables, migrations, and one-row test inputs.
Verifies workflows and produces diagrams before effectful runs.
Runs, inspects, cancels, and queries saved workflows through the GTM CLI.
Adds schedule metadata and supports local or hosted deployment workflows.
Tracks run results, workflow rows, and paid-call cost records.
limitations: It is for reusable saved workflows, not one-time analysis or workspace setup.
Hosted deployment requires a configured production URL and required credentials.
Agentic stages require supported provider configuration and explicit spend limits.
The generated project and its dependencies require separate review before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a lead enrichment workflow
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable workflow that validates rows, enriches records, and stores results after a one-row test.

use_cases.title: Operate a deployed workflow
use_cases.description: Inspect recent runs, query stored results, approve a checkpoint, or cancel an active workflow.

use_cases.title: Maintain workflow infrastructure
use_cases.description: Add a migration, update a schedule, verify deployment readiness, and prepare a controlled release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable workflow that validates a small list of leads. Include a one-row test and explain the approval needed before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the latest run for the lead-enrichment workflow. Summarize its status, cost, completed rows, and failures.

prompt_templates.title: Add a safe schedule
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a weekday schedule to the account-refresh workflow. Verify the workflow and show the external effects before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Update with controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the enrichment workflow to add an agentic research stage. Set a per-row spend cap, add Diagram cost metadata, test one row, and request approval before deployment.

output_examples.input: Create a workflow for a small lead list.
output: Workflow plan with inputs, result table, and one-row test
Approval card describing saved changes, cost, and external effects
Verification result and workflow diagram after testing

output_examples.input: Check the latest deployed workflow run.
output: Recorded cost and row outcome counts
Plain-language failure reason when a run does not complete

best_practices: Use a one-row test and review its projected cost before every new workflow run.
Keep credentials in environment variables and do not commit local data or environment files.
Review migration effects and request fresh approval when costs or external effects change.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for one-off work that should not become a reusable workflow.
Do not run a full workflow before verification and explicit approval.
Do not store secrets, test data, or generated runtime files in version control.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages saved GTM workflow code, result tables, migrations, runs, schedules, diagrams, and deployment metadata.

faq.question: Does it run workflows without approval?
faq.answer: No. It prepares and verifies work first, then requests approval before effectful runs, deployment, cancellation, or similar actions.

faq.question: Can it work locally?
faq.answer: Yes. The template can start a loopback server when needed for a local workflow run.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Requirements depend on the workflow and provider. Credentials remain in environment variables rather than workflow files.

faq.question: How are costs controlled?
faq.answer: The workflow uses Diagram metadata, per-stage limits, and a one-row test to show projected paid-call costs before a larger run.

faq.question: Is this suitable for Codex?
faq.answer: Codex supports the workflow lifecycle, but agentic stages need an AI key because Codex cannot enforce the same spend-cap behavior.
